text:
emily: hey all, i'm in my first week and trying to get secrets set up for my dev env. i created a service account but `vault kv get` returns 403. who handles granting dev-only read for onboarding?

ryan: welcome! :wave: dev access goes through the Access form (https://redwood.internal/selfservice). choose 'Dev - Vault read (onboarding)' and include your OKTA email + service account. that queues ops for review.

emily: i tried that, ticket says waiting. any quick workaround to peek at a non-prod secret for a demo?

kate: ops can issue a one-hour read token if you include a demo link and time window. ping ops in the ticket and tag me. we avoid giving wide policies.

secrets-bot: Ticket VAULT-5102 created for emily. Estimated review 1 business day.

ryan: note we use KV v2, path is secret/data/<path>. sample:
``
vault kv get secret/data/team/emily/dev
```
for writing:
``
vault kv put secret/team/emily/dev api_key=xxx
```

emily: thanks. about rotation: if i rotate an API key in Vault, do clients pick up automatically?

kate: clients must handle reloading. we recommend using the transit engine or a short-lived token pattern. for long-lived API keys rotate 30-90 days depending on type. we also add a versioned tag in CI so deploys can trigger reloads.

ryan: infra folks can provision secrets via terraform in CI. example:
``
resource "vault_kv_secret_v2" "dev_key" {
  mount = "secret"
  name  = "team/emily/dev"
  data_json = jsonencode({ api_key = var.api_key })
}
```
ensure your pipeline uses the `ci-vault-role` with limited write.

emily: got it. what's the relationship with cloud KMS? do we ever store raw keys?

kate: raw root keys live in cloud KMS. Vault stores encrypted blobs or uses transit backed by a KMS-wrapped key. we don't put unwrapped long-term root keys in Vault.

secrets-bot: Reminder: Vault admin roles require MFA.

emily: excellent, thanks for the help. i'll update the ticket with my demo time and tag kate. :smile:
